chunks: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, has included the two parents against all those entitled to the obligatory shares, so He has not reduced the two of them below one-sixth, for each one of the two; and He has included the husband and the wife against all those entitled to the inheritances, so He has not reduced the two of them below the quarter and the eighth.

key_terms.الثُّمُنِ: Al-Thumn — one-eighth (1/8), the wife's minimum share when there are children
key_terms.الرُّبُعِ: Al-Rub' — one-quarter (1/4), the husband's minimum share when there are children
key_terms.السُّدُسِ: Al-Sudus — one-sixth (1/6), the minimum guaranteed share for each parent
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: Fara'id — the divinely mandated obligatory shares in inheritance law
key_terms.الْمَوَارِيثِ: Al-Mawarith — inheritances; the general pool from which all heirs receive their shares

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum guaranteed shares for parents and spouses in Islamic inheritance law according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) explains a foundational principle of Islamic inheritance law: that God has guaranteed minimum shares for the parents and for spouses. The parents are guaranteed at least one-sixth each regardless of other heirs, and the husband and wife are guaranteed their minimum shares (one-quarter and one-eighth respectively) regardless of who else inherits. This ruling is rooted in Quran 4:11-12, which establishes the fara'id (obligatory shares), and it addresses the principle of 'awl (proportional reduction) — the parents and spouses cannot be reduced below their Quranic minima.
